planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; this triploid species does not reproduce by spore in cultivation, so propagation is by division only.

directions: An East Asian evergreen wood fern from China, Japan, and Korea, prized for glossy, triangular, light-green fronds that catch the light differently than the darker evergreen Dryopteris already in cultivation. It is a triploid, meaning it sets no viable spore, so every plant in the trade traces back to vegetative division, a useful detail for gardeners trying to source or propagate it correctly. Give it humus-rich, well-drained soil in part sun to light shade, and expect steady but unhurried clump expansion over several years.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade; evergreen to semi-evergreen in milder winters.

directions: A Korean, Chinese, and Japanese wood fern with finely cut, lacy fronds, evergreen to semi-evergreen depending on winter severity, giving a different texture than the broader-leaved Dryopteris already in the collection. It wants consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade and spreads at a moderate pace to form an attractive colony over time. Good as a textural companion planted among coarser-leaved hostas or heucheras in a woodland bed.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in well-drained, humus-rich soil in bright shade; black, glossy stems and stiff silvery fronds show best out of harsh midday sun.

directions: A Chinese evergreen shield fern with stiff, silvery-shiny fronds and glossy black stems, giving it a metallic sheen distinct from the typical matte green of most Polystichum already grown. It wants bright shade rather than deep shade to show its best color, along with well-drained, humus-rich soil. Use it as a specimen in a shaded rock garden or trough where its distinctive silver sheen can be appreciated up close.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in light shade; the creeping rhizome is well-behaved and not invasive, so clumps expand slowly and predictably.

directions: A Japanese evergreen fern with large, arching, finely divided fronds that give it a bold, almost tropical presence in a shade garden well outside the true tropics. Its creeping rhizome expands at a well-behaved, non-invasive pace, making it suitable for a woodland border where a bigger textural statement is wanted without the fern taking over. Give it moist, humus-rich soil in light shade and protection from the hottest afternoon sun.
